officialTitle: Tarlatamab for Patients with Previously Treated Small-Cell Lung Cancer

design.blinding: Open-label; objective response by blinded independent central review
design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Overall, 220 patients received tarlatamab; patients had previously received a median of two lines of treatment.
design.notes: Phase 2 evaluation of two tarlatamab dose levels without a comparator arm; the abstract does not describe how patients were allocated between dose groups. Efficacy results are descriptive and not comparative.

clinicalQuestion: What is the antitumour activity and safety of the DLL3-directed bispecific T-cell engager tarlatamab in previously treated SCLC, and which dose should be taken forward?

pico.intervention: Tarlatamab 10 mg or 100 mg intravenously every 2 weeks
pico.outcomes: Primary: objective response by BICR. Secondary: DoR, PFS, OS, safety

arms.label: Tarlatamab 10 mg
arms.doseSourceQuote: we evaluated the antitumor activity and safety of tarlatamab, administered intravenously every 2 weeks at a dose of 10 mg or 100 mg

arms.label: Tarlatamab 100 mg
arms.doseSourceQuote: we evaluated the antitumor activity and safety of tarlatamab, administered intravenously every 2 weeks at a dose of 10 mg or 100 mg

publications.title: Tarlatamab for Patients with Previously Treated Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.population: Patients evaluated for antitumour activity, 10 mg group
outcomes.sourceQuote: An objective response occurred in 40% (97.5% confidence interval [CI], 29 to 52) of the patients in the 10-mg group and in 32% (97.5% CI, 21 to 44) of those in the 100-mg group.

outcomes.population: Patients evaluated for antitumour activity, 100 mg group
outcomes.sourceQuote: An objective response occurred in 40% (97.5% confidence interval [CI], 29 to 52) of the patients in the 10-mg group and in 32% (97.5% CI, 21 to 44) of those in the 100-mg group.

outcomes.endpointLabel: Duration of response at least 6 months
outcomes.sourceQuote: Among patients with an objective response, the duration of response was at least 6 months in 59% (40 of 68 patients).
The median progression-free survival was 4.9 months (95% CI, 2.9 to 6.7) in the 10-mg group and 3.9 months (95% CI, 2.6 to 4.4) in the 100-mg group

the estimates of overall survival at 9 months were 68% and 66% of patients, respectively.

safety.description: Cytokine-release syndrome, any grade (10 mg vs 100 mg)
safety.sourceQuote: The most common adverse events were cytokine-release syndrome (in 51% of the patients in the 10-mg group and in 61% of those in the 100-mg group)

safety.description: Grade 3 cytokine-release syndrome (10 mg vs 100 mg)
safety.sourceQuote: Grade 3 cytokine-release syndrome occurred less frequently in the 10-mg group (in 1% of the patients) than in the 100-mg group (in 6%).

safety.description: Discontinuation due to treatment-related adverse events (all patients)
safety.sourceQuote: A low percentage of patients (3%) discontinued tarlatamab because of treatment-related adverse events.

strengths: Objective response assessed by blinded independent central review
Durable responses in a heavily pretreated population with few options
limitations: Phase 2 without a comparator arm; efficacy is descriptive and cannot establish superiority over chemotherapy
Cytokine-release syndrome requires monitoring during early cycles
Patient selection by DLL3 expression is not described in the abstract

clinicalImplications.text: Showed durable responses with tarlatamab at the lower dose in previously treated SCLC, establishing the dose taken into the randomised DeLLphi-304 comparison against chemotherapy.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Cytokine-release syndrome clusters in the first cycle and is mostly low grade; plan monitored initiation.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 37861218. The 100 mg cohort is recorded in safety controlValue fields for side-by-side display only; it is not a control arm.
